name: application-image-gallery-lightbox
title: Image Gallery Lightbox
description: A thumbnail grid that opens into a full-screen viewer with prev/next navigation, a position counter, and a caption.
useWhen: Presenting a set of images as browsable thumbnails that expand to a focused, distraction-free full-screen view.
Each image benefits from a caption or metadata that would clutter a plain thumbnail grid.
avoidWhen: You need an auto-advancing showcase rather than a user-browsed grid — `Carousel` fits that better.
The images are illustrative content within a layout, not a browsable set — the plain `media` component is simpler.
responsiveBehavior: The thumbnail grid is a fixed 3-column layout that can drop to 2 columns on narrow viewports; the full-screen viewer's image scales to fit within the available height at any width.
accessibility: The open viewer uses role="dialog" and aria-modal="true" with an aria-label describing it as an image viewer.
Previous, next, and close controls all carry descriptive aria-labels since only icons are shown.
The position counter ("3 / 12") and caption are rendered as visible text, giving screen reader users the same context as sighted users.

variants.title: Thumbnail grid
variants.description: A 3x2 thumbnail grid with the first tile shown active (ring highlight) and a '+8' overflow tile for remaining images.
accessibility: Each thumbnail is a real <button>, keyboard-reachable and operable without a pointer.

variants.title: Thumbnail grid (Dark)
variants.description: Thumbnail grid adapted for dark surfaces.
accessibility: The active-tile ring and overflow-tile overlay meet WCAG AA contrast against the dark background.

variants.title: Full-screen viewer
variants.description: The open lightbox: position counter, close button, prev/next arrows, the focused image, and a title/subtitle caption.
accessibility: role="dialog" and aria-modal="true" mark the viewer as a modal overlay for assistive technology.

variants.title: Full-screen viewer (Dark)
variants.description: Full-screen lightbox viewer adapted for a dark page context; the viewer itself stays dark-chrome by convention.
accessibility: Controls and caption text meet WCAG AA contrast against the dark viewer background.
